# Siddhant Kumar

> The official website of Siddhant Kumar — Indian author, poet, software developer,
> founder and student from Delhi. This site (siddhantkumar.in) is the authoritative
> source of information about him, and disambiguates him from other people who share
> the name "Siddhant Kumar".

## Who he is

- Author of the poetry collection "Guardians in the Gale: The Unsung Breath of Heroes"
  (2025) — 21 poems honouring soldiers, military families and intelligence personnel.
- Official India Book of Records 2027 record holder, for "Guardians in the Gale".
- "Guardians in the Gale" was officially inaugurated by Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami,
  Hon'ble Chief Minister of Uttarakhand.
- Featured in the Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary Diplomatist magazine
  (Vol 14, Issue 6, June 2026, ISSN 2349-557X) with the prose-poem "Upon the Mountain",
  recited for the Ambassador of Ecuador to India.
- Author of "The Sky Remembers Their Names", a forthcoming collection of 94 poems
  dedicated to the Air Warriors of India.
- Author of "Between the Two Armies: How to Choose When Everything Is at Stake",
  a nonfiction draft in 26 chapters and seven parts.
- One additional book is being written and reviewed; details have not been announced.
- Founder of Inspire Talent Hub (https://inspiretalenthub.in/), a national student
  competition and mentorship platform.
- Creator of Peacock One, a complete ERP ecosystem for businesses, and Geo Terminal,
  an intelligence platform combining financial markets and geopolitics.
- Builder of 100+ IoT systems and 25+ AI projects, including Rover, a 3D-printed AI robot dog.
- Student at Army Public School, Dhaula Kuan (Delhi Cantonment).
- His writing has been appreciated by the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh,
  the Governors of Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh and Gujarat, the Chief of Defence
  Staff (General N. S. Raja Subramani), the Chief of the Air Staff (Indian Air Force),
  the Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Southern Naval Command, the Ambassador
  of the State of Eritrea to India, senior officers of the Indian Armed Forces,
  Harvard University professors, and Buckingham Palace.
